civics: Ancient Romans followed written laws such as the Twelve Tables, an early example of the idea that leaders are not above the law. Name this principle.
Rule of law
Name the idea that citizens should elect representatives to govern, in contrast to rule by a hereditary monarch.
Republicanism
Which English philosopher taught that legitimate government depends on the consent of the governed?
John Locke
Which French thinker argued for separating government power, an idea that shaped the three branches of the U.S. government?
Montesquieu
Which writer attacked monarchy and urged colonists toward independence in the pamphlet Common Sense?
Thomas Paine
Colonists objected to British soldiers being lodged in their homes. Name this grievance.
Quartering troops
Colonists believed Britain was taking away an important legal protection when it limited which kind of trial?
Trial by jury
The king interfered with colonial self-government by dissolving which colonial bodies?
Colonial legislatures
Name the document written to explain to the world why the colonies were separating from the British Empire.
Declaration of Independence
The Declaration of Independence calls fundamental rights that government should not take away by what name?
Unalienable rights
Besides life and liberty, which unalienable right does the Declaration of Independence name?
The pursuit of happiness
Name the first plan of national government, which had no executive branch, no standing army, and no effective power to tax.
Articles of Confederation
The Constitution fixed the lack of an executive under the Articles by creating which office?
The President
Under the Articles the national government could not raise money effectively. Which power did the Constitution give Congress to fix this?
The power to tax
Name the opening paragraph of the Constitution that lists its goals, beginning with We the People.
The Preamble
Which Preamble goal means keeping peace and order inside the country?
Insure domestic Tranquility
Which Preamble goal means protecting the nation from outside threats?
Provide for the common defense
Which Preamble goal means uniting the states more fully under one effective government?
Form a more perfect Union
Which Preamble goal means protecting freedom for the people and their posterity?
Secure the Blessings of Liberty
Which Preamble goal means supporting the well-being of the country and its people?
Promote the general Welfare
Which Preamble goal means creating a fair system of laws and government?
Establish Justice
Name the system in which each branch can limit the others so that no branch becomes too powerful.
Checks and balances
The President may negotiate a treaty, but which chamber of Congress can refuse to ratify it?
The Senate
In 1974 the Supreme Court ordered a President to turn over Watergate evidence, showing the President is not above the law. Name this case.
United States v. Nixon
Name the group that supported ratifying the Constitution and wanted a stronger national government.
Federalists
Name the group that feared a powerful national government and demanded a Bill of Rights.
Anti-Federalists
Obeying laws, paying taxes, and serving on a jury when summoned are legally required. Are these obligations or responsibilities?
Obligations
Joining a political party is voluntary civic participation. Is it an obligation or a responsibility?
A responsibility
Name the legal process by which an immigrant becomes a United States citizen.
Naturalization
Citizens elect representatives, a constitution limits the government, and individual rights are protected. Name this form of government.
Constitutional republic
Political power is concentrated in a few hands and individual freedoms are limited. Name this form of government.
Authoritarian
In Saudi Arabia a king inherits power and appoints officials. Name this form of government.
Monarchy
Power is shared between the national government and the states, as in the United States. Name this system of government.
Federal
The central government holds the main authority and local governments receive their power from it. Name this system of government.
Unitary
Member states hold most of the power and the central government is weak. Name this system of government.
Confederal
Which branch of government makes federal laws and holds the power to coin money?
Legislative branch (Congress)
Which official enforces federal laws, can pardon federal crimes, and serves as Commander-in-Chief?
The President
Which article of the Constitution describes the judicial branch?
Article III
Powers specifically listed for the national government in the Constitution are called what?
Enumerated powers
Powers that the Constitution does not give to the national government and that the states keep are called what?
Reserved powers
Powers shared by the national and state governments, such as collecting taxes, are called what?
Concurrent powers
Name the 1803 case that established judicial review, the power of courts to strike down unconstitutional laws.
Marbury v. Madison
Name the 1857 case in which the Supreme Court ruled that enslaved people and their descendants were not citizens.
Dred Scott v. Sandford
Name the 1896 case that upheld racial segregation under the doctrine of separate but equal.
Plessy v. Ferguson
Name the 1954 case that ruled segregated public schools unconstitutional.
Brown v. Board of Education
Name the 1963 case requiring states to provide a lawyer to criminal defendants who cannot afford one.
Gideon v. Wainwright
Name the 1966 case requiring police to warn suspects of their right to remain silent and to have an attorney.
Miranda v. Arizona
Name the 1967 case that gave juveniles accused of crimes due process rights such as notice of charges and a lawyer.
In re Gault
Name the 1988 case allowing school officials to censor school-sponsored student newspapers.
Hazelwood v. Kuhlmeier
general: This planet's Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth, and Galileo discovered four of its moons. Name this largest planet in the solar system.
Jupiter
Which British author created the detective Hercule Poirot and wrote And Then There Were None?
Agatha Christie
Name the organelle that contains its own DNA and is the site of cellular respiration.
Mitochondrion
Name the 1919 treaty, signed in the Hall of Mirrors, that ended the First World War between Germany and the Allies.
Treaty of Versailles
Which German composer wrote nine symphonies, the last ending with the Ode to Joy, after losing his hearing?
Ludwig van Beethoven
Which South American river flows across Brazil and carries more water than any other river on Earth?
Amazon River
Name the quantity equal to mass times velocity that is conserved in collisions.
Momentum
Which Dutch painter created The Starry Night while staying at an asylum in Saint-Rémy?
Vincent van Gogh
Which element makes up about 78 percent of Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen
In which Shakespeare tragedy does a Danish prince hold the skull of the jester Yorick?
Hamlet
Name the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing, built for the pharaoh Khufu.
Great Pyramid of Giza
Which country has Canberra as its capital and Uluru in its outback?
Australia
Which English naturalist developed natural selection after a voyage on HMS Beagle?
Charles Darwin
Name the Harper Lee novel in which Atticus Finch defends Tom Robinson in Alabama.
To Kill a Mockingbird
Name the process in which chloroplasts turn light, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and oxygen.
Photosynthesis
Which French leader crowned himself emperor in 1804 and was defeated at Waterloo?
Napoleon Bonaparte
Which Renaissance artist painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling and carved the statue David?
Michelangelo
Name the mountain on the Nepal and China border that rises higher above sea level than any other.
Mount Everest
Which Greek hero spent ten years sailing home to Ithaca after the Trojan War?
Odysseus
Name the NASA program whose eleventh mission landed Neil Armstrong on the Moon.
Apollo program
